y877a565e08f.add: - **Oxytocin** is a **peptide hormone** (9 amino acids, from the hypothalamus, released by the posterior pituitary), not counted as a protein; keratin, fibroin and collagen are structural proteins.

y0c48012e758.add: - **Vitamin B6 and dreams:** a 2018 Univ. of Adelaide study found B6 supplements improved **dream recall** (remembering dreams).

yd54faa9637c.add: - **Milk** has several **B vitamins** (riboflavin B2, B12) and calcium but is poor in **vitamin C** and **iron**.

y4d869f00c78.add: - **Not genetic:** **night blindness** and **xerophthalmia** (vitamin A deficiency); **genetic:** albinism, haemophilia, colour blindness, Down's syndrome.

y284f6865448.add: - **Xerophthalmia** (vitamin A deficiency, leading cause of preventable child blindness) is India's priority deficiency – the National Prophylaxis Programme gives children vitamin A doses (UPSC 1996).

y4c1a36be716.add: - **Alpha-keratin** – skin (epidermis), hair, nails, horns, wool; **beta-keratin** – feathers, scales.

y775c0d6a8ad.add: - **Vitamin B12** is water-soluble yet **stored in the liver for 3–5 years** – the exception to 'water-soluble vitamins are not stored'.

y6c60c9d7e60.add: - **Vitamin K** is the **antidote** to warfarin-type **anticoagulant** poisons (rat poisons) – it restores clotting-factor synthesis.

y7105961f0a3.add: - **DNA** contains the bases **adenine, guanine, cytosine, thymine** (+ sugar, phosphate); **tyrosine** is an amino acid, not part of DNA.

y5ce8816fbc2.add: - **Rayon** (regenerated cellulose from wood pulp) = **artificial silk**; **acrylic** = artificial wool; **polycarbonate** – CDs; cotton – summer clothing (absorbs sweat).

yf0fbfaed7bc.add: - The body **cannot make vitamin A** itself (it comes from food retinol or carotene); proteins, enzymes and hormones are made in the body.

y909539c99ee.add: - **Alzheimer's disease:** plaques of **amyloid-beta**, cut from **amyloid precursor protein (APP)**, plus tau tangles.

ye1e2b249cf1.add: - **Enzymes** are biological catalysts and are **mostly proteins** (a few RNA enzymes – ribozymes).

y6eb4b772648.add: - **Exercise fuel:** carbohydrate (muscle glycogen, blood glucose) is the main fuel of hard and endurance exercise; in **prolonged low-moderate** exercise **fat** supplies ~50% or more.

yd6fcf671d53.add: - Enzymes are basically **proteins** – e.g. pepsin, trypsin, amylase (not fats, sugars or vitamins).

y99606ae8cb7.add: - **Ascorbic acid** has **no –COOH group** (its acidity is from an enol –OH in a lactone ring); citric, lactic and tartaric acids are carboxylic acids.

yaee7f767fe8.add: - **Human mineral needs:** **phosphorus** (bones, ATP, DNA), **zinc** (enzymes, immunity), trace **cobalt** (in vitamin B12) – all three needed.

y15199b99b2b.add: - **Balanced (healthy) diet:** an **optimal** mix of carbohydrate, protein and fat with **adequate water and roughage (fibre)**, plus vitamins and minerals.

y7e74f98d3ea.add: - **ATP** (adenosine triphosphate) = the **energy currency** of the cell; glucose is the fuel, pyruvic acid the product of glycolysis.

ya7e6d8cb7f8.add: - **Gout:** uric acid (end product of **purine** breakdown from **nucleic acids**) builds up in joints – patients limit purine-rich food (organ meat, some seafood).

y90fe7370549.add: - **Hypokalemia** = low blood **potassium** (kalium); low iodine – goitre, low iron – anaemia, low calcium – hypocalcaemia.

yfca1d065a4c.add: - **Bones and teeth** are mainly **calcium phosphate** (hydroxyapatite) – calcium and phosphorus are needed.

y63009c89477.add: - **Taste of starch:** starch itself is almost tasteless; on chewing, **salivary amylase** turns it into **maltose**, so starchy food (and carbohydrates generally) taste **sweet**.

y491c1ff2c5f.add: - **Plant pigments:** **lycopene** – red of tomato; **carotene** – orange (carrot); **lutein** – **yellow** xanthophyll (marigold, egg yolk, eye macula); anthocyanin – red/purple/blue; capsaicin – pungency of chilli (not a colour).

y66943406ca7.add: - **Tomato red = lycopene** (a carotenoid); capsaicin gives chilli its heat.

yeadd51d4798.add: - **Iron sources:** green leafy vegetables (**spinach**), liver, jaggery, dates (carrot – vitamin A; pea – protein).

y569b7536e14.add: - **Karonda** (*Carissa carandas*) is the fruit noted as a **rich iron source** (used against anaemia), also rich in vitamin C.

y28083558bf5.add: - **Milk and vitamin A:** books treat milk as **poor in vitamin A** (and C, iron); carrot, mango, papaya are the carotene sources.

y64e2a6861ba.add: - **Protein needs with age:** older adults need **more** protein per kg (1.0–1.2 g/kg, PROT-AGE) than young adults (0.8 g/kg) to prevent muscle loss.

y103b5bc8c91.add: - **Milk minerals:** rich in **calcium and potassium** (and phosphorus) but very **poor in iron**.

yf2b216b176e.add: - **Potassium deficiency:** muscle weakness, cramps, **paralysis**, irregular heartbeat; books also list **low blood pressure** (exam key), though low potassium more often raises BP.

y5b248bf8295.add: - The body **cannot make most vitamins** (exceptions: D in skin, K and B12 by gut bacteria, niacin from tryptophan) – they must come from food; vitamins **do not kill bacteria**.

y8c126068317.add: - **Unsaturated fats** have **C=C double bonds**, so they are more reactive (oxidise, go rancid, can be hydrogenated); saturated fats have only single bonds.

y1401c36c067.add: - **Hypothalamus** = the body's **thermostat** – controls body temperature, hunger, thirst; links nervous and endocrine systems.

y94917f36580.add: - **Albuminuria** (albumin in urine) signals **kidney** malfunction (damaged glomeruli hold back albumin normally).

y26a61fd9314.add: - **Ascites** = fluid in the **peritoneal (abdominal) cavity**; hydrothorax – pleural cavity; hydroamnion – excess amniotic fluid; oedema – tissues.

y08409cda030.add: - **Salivary glands:** parotid (largest), submandibular, sublingual; the **pineal** is an endocrine gland in the brain.

y90b57346915.add: - **Skin** = the **largest organ** of the body; **liver** = largest **gland** (internal organ).

yd902ba350a0.add: - **Litmus:** a **base** turns **red litmus blue**; an **acid** turns **blue litmus red**; neutral salt changes neither.

y2703395b81d.add: - **Liver functions:** secretes **bile**, **metabolises drugs** and toxins, regulates blood chemicals (glucose, proteins), stores **glycogen**, makes urea.

y739e06c202c.add: - **'Thermostat' of the body = hypothalamus**; cerebellum – balance; hippocampus – memory; frontal lobe – reasoning.

ya8941418374.add: - **Kidney** is the most commonly **transplanted organ** (living or deceased donor).

ye5c227355dd.add: - **Adam's apple** = the projecting **thyroid cartilage of the larynx** (voice box), larger in males after puberty.

ybfea540976f.add: - **Glycogen** = the storage carbohydrate of animals ('animal starch'); plants store **starch**.

yb35b134b2ee.add: - **Nephron** = the structural and functional (excretory) unit of the **kidney** (~1 million per kidney).

y9e9a0a02934.add: - **Liver and skeletal muscle** store **glycogen** as the energy reserve (pepsinogen = inactive pepsin).

y9c4eb5b8dcc.add: - A normal human body cell has **46 chromosomes (23 pairs)**: 44 autosomes + 2 sex chromosomes.

ybb24289ebaa.add: - **Hepatocytes** = the main cells of the **liver** (hepar = liver); neurons – brain; cardiomyocytes – heart.
